Divide paper into five parts:
- Preliminary Data Science
- Feature Selection
- Base Model Creation
- Feature Selected Model Creation
- Model Comparison

# 1. PRELIMINARY ACTIONS

Goals: Get lung cancer dataset ready for modeling and perform exploratory data analysis

## a. Data Cleaning for Modeling

```{r}
# --- PACKAGES ---

# Clear environment
remove(list=ls())

# Starter libraries (new ones will be added as used)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(rsample) # Data split
library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)
library(pROC) # ROC curves
library(randomForest)
```

```{r}
# --- GET DATA ---
lung_cancer <- read.csv("final_dataset.csv")
```

The data was preprocessed so that no NA values are present, potentially significant columns are chosen, and all instances of observations diagnosed with lung cancer are included in our dataset along with a proportional, matched group of non-cancer instances, which were found using the nonparametric matching system MatchIt.

```{r}
# --- INITIAL DATA CLEANING ---
lung_cancer <- lung_cancer %>%
  select(!X) %>% # Remove column number from download
  select(!SEQNO) %>% # Remove observation ID
  mutate(GENDER = ifelse(GENDER == "Male", 1, 0), # Change gender to binary feature
         LUNG_CANCER = as.factor(ifelse(LUNG_CANCER == 1, "Yes", "No")), # Change lung cancer indicator to Yes/No for models
         AGE_GROUP = as.factor(AGE_GROUP)) # Change age group indicator to factor 
```

```{r}
# --- DATA SUMMARY ---
summary(lung_cancer)
```

## b. Exploratory Data Analysis

The next two code chunks replicate a visualization made by our parent paper, which plots how much of each age group had lung cancer or not.

```{r}
# --- OBTAIN LUNG CANCER PREVALENCE BY AGE GROUP ---
age_group_pct <- lung_cancer %>%
  group_by(AGE_GROUP, LUNG_CANCER) %>%
  summarize(Count = n(),
            Ratio = Count / nrow(lung_cancer))
```

```{r}
# --- PLOT LUNG CANCER PREVALENCE BY AGE GROUP
ggplot(data=age_group_pct, aes(x=AGE_GROUP, y=Count, fill=LUNG_CANCER)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("No" = "steelblue", "Yes" = "#ED7D31")) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of Lung Cancer by Age Group",
       subtitle = "Based on matched sample, non-representative of population",
       x = "Age Group", y = "Count", fill = "Lung Cancer?") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The next chunk generates a correlation plot to check possible blocks to significance.

```{r}
library(ggcorrplot)

model.matrix(~0+., data=lung_cancer %>% select(!AGE_GROUP)) %>% 
  cor(use="pairwise.complete.obs") %>% 
  ggcorrplot(show.diag=FALSE, type="lower", lab=TRUE, lab_size=1.5)
```

Since smoking ever has a 100% correlation with smoking in the last 100 days, we can remove SMOKE100 from our analysis so that there is no noise preventing smoking from being potentially significant.

```{r}
# SMOKE100 is, for the purposes of modeling, the same variable as SMOKER
# BMI plays directly into height and weight, removing HEIGHT and WEIGHT as well
model_data <- lung_cancer %>%
  select(!SMOKE100) %>%
  select(!HEIGHT) %>%
  select(!WEIGHT)
```

# 2. FEATURE SELECTION

Goal: Create multiple metrics pointing us towards significant features to select

## a. Random Forest and Gain Ratio

The random forest score is calculated using Gini.

```{r}
# --- RANDOM FOREST ---
set.seed(123)

# Make a random forest model
rf_model <- randomForest(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = model_data,
  importance = TRUE,
  ntree = 500
)

# Obtain importance scores
rf_importance <- importance(rf_model, type = 2) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Feature") %>%
  rename(RF_Ranking = MeanDecreaseGini) %>%
  arrange(desc(RF_Ranking))

rf_importance
```

The code below creates the Gain Ratio function.

```{r}
# --- GAIN RATIO ---
# Formula: GR(f_i) = [H(c) - H(c|f_i)] / H(f_i)

# Entropy function: H(X) = -sum(p * log2(p))
entropy <- function(x) {
  probs <- table(x) / length(x)
  probs <- probs[probs > 0]  # avoid log(0)
  -sum(probs * log2(probs))
}

# Conditional entropy function: H(c|f) = sum over f's values of P(f=v) * H(c | f=v)
conditional_entropy <- function(class_var, feature_var) {
  levels_f <- unique(feature_var)
  total_n <- length(feature_var)
  cond_h <- 0
  for (v in levels_f) {
    subset_class <- class_var[feature_var == v]
    weight <- length(subset_class) / total_n
    cond_h <- cond_h + weight * entropy(subset_class)
  }
  return(cond_h)
}

# Gain Ratio function for one feature
gain_ratio_single <- function(class_var, feature_var) {
  h_c <- entropy(class_var)
  h_c_given_f <- conditional_entropy(class_var, feature_var)
  h_f <- entropy(feature_var)
  info_gain <- h_c - h_c_given_f
  
  # Avoid divide-by-zero if feature has only 1 unique value
  if (h_f == 0) {return(0)}
  gr <- info_gain / h_f
  return(gr)
}
```

The code below implements Gain Ratio.

```{r}
# Obtain feature names
feature_names <- setdiff(names(model_data), "LUNG_CANCER")
class_var <- model_data$LUNG_CANCER

# Apply gain ratio scores
gr_scores <- sapply(feature_names, function(f) {
  gain_ratio_single(class_var, model_data[[f]])
})

# Create data frame for gain ratio scores
gain_ratio_result <- data.frame(
  Feature = names(gr_scores),
  GR_Ranking = round(as.numeric(gr_scores), 4)
) %>%
  arrange(desc(GR_Ranking))

gain_ratio_result
```

The code below combines both metrics into a table.

```{r}
feature_rankings <- rf_importance %>%
  left_join(gain_ratio_result, by=join_by("Feature"=="Feature"))
```

## b. Forwards Elimination

Goal: Create a base model, a finished full model, and work our way between.

```{r}
library(stats)

# Base model with only intercept
base_model <- glm(LUNG_CANCER ~ 1, family = binomial, data = model_data)

# Full model with all potential predictors
full_model <- glm(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., family = binomial, data = model_data)
```

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Forward elimination
forwards_elim <- stats::step(object = base_model,
                             scope = list(lower = base_model, upper = full_model),
                             data = model_data,
                             direction = "forward")
```

```{r}
forwards_elim$coefficients
```

## c. Backwards Selection

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Backwards elimination
backwards_elim <- stats::step(object = full_model,
                              scope = formula(full_model),
                              data = model_data,
                              direction = "backward",
                              trace = 0)

```

```{r}
backwards_elim$coefficients
```

## Summary Table

```{r}
# 1 (Yes) or 0 (No): Were the variables from Gain Ratio table chosen by each selection model?
forwards_chosen  <- c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No")
backwards_chosen <- c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No")

feature_rankings <- feature_rankings %>%
  mutate(ForwardSelect = forwards_chosen,
         BackwardSelect = backwards_chosen)
```

```{r}
kable(feature_rankings, 
      col.names = c("Feature", "Random Forest Score", "Gain Ratio Score", "Forwards Selection", "Backwards Selection"),
      align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"))
```

Our selected features will be the five that feature in the top six of both random forest and gain ratio, and the five which were selected by both models: BMI, COPD, POOR_PHYS_DAYS, SMOKER, EXERCISE

```{r}
selected_data <- model_data %>%
  select(LUNG_CANCER, COPD, SMOKER, POOR_PHYS_DAYS, BMI, EXERCISE)
```


# 3. MODELS WITHOUT FEATURE SELECTION

```{r}
# General
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)
library(pROC) # ROC curves

# ML Model Packages

library(discretization) # For supervised discretization (MDLP method)

library(e1071) # SVM
```

## Data Split

```{r}
set.seed(123)

split <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), nrow(model_data), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.75, 0.25))

train_set <- model_data[split, ]
test_set <- model_data[!split, ]

train_selected <- selected_data[split, ]
test_selected <- selected_data[!split, ]
```

## Create Training Controls

```{r}
set.seed(123)
cv_folds <- createFolds(train_set$LUNG_CANCER, k = 10, returnTrain = TRUE)

train_ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  index = cv_folds,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  verboseIter = FALSE
)
```

## Naive Bayes

```{r}
symptom_cols <- c("COPD", "ASTHMA", "SMOKER", "AGE_GROUP", "GENDER", 
                  "EXERCISE", "ECIGS", "SMOKELESS_TOBACCO", "COVID19")

for (col in symptom_cols) {
  train_set[[col]] <- factor(train_set[[col]])
  test_set[[col]]  <- factor(test_set[[col]], levels = levels(train_set[[col]]))
}

nb_grid <- expand.grid(
  laplace = c(0, 1, 2),
  usekernel = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  adjust = c(1, 1.5)
)

set.seed(123)
nb_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ ., 
  data = train_set,
  method = "naive_bayes",
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  tuneGrid = nb_grid,
  metric = "ROC"
)

nb_preds <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_set)
confusionMatrix(nb_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
```

## Bayesian Network (BayesNet)

```{r}
library(bnlearn)
library(pROC)
library(caret)

# 1. Prepare data frames
train_bn <- train_set
test_bn  <- test_set

# Ensure BMI is numeric before discretizing
train_bn$BMI <- as.numeric(train_bn$BMI)
test_bn$BMI  <- as.numeric(test_bn$BMI)

# Factorize all other categorical/symptom columns
factor_cols <- setdiff(names(train_bn), c("BMI", "LUNG_CANCER"))
train_bn[factor_cols] <- lapply(train_bn[factor_cols], factor)
test_bn[factor_cols]  <- lapply(test_bn[factor_cols], factor)

# 2. Discretize BMI into 3 quantile bins using bnlearn
train_bn["BMI"] <- bnlearn::discretize(
  data = train_bn["BMI"],
  method = "quantile",
  breaks = 3,
  ordered = FALSE
)

# Project training quantile boundaries onto test_set$BMI
raw_train_vals <- as.numeric(train_set$BMI)
brks <- quantile(raw_train_vals, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 4), na.rm = TRUE)
brks[1] <- -Inf
brks[length(brks)] <- Inf

test_bn$BMI <- cut(
  as.numeric(test_set$BMI),
  breaks = brks,
  labels = levels(train_bn$BMI),
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

# Ensure test_bn factor levels match train_bn perfectly
for (col in names(train_bn)) {
  if (is.factor(train_bn[[col]])) {
    test_bn[[col]] <- factor(test_bn[[col]], levels = levels(train_bn[[col]]))
  }
}

target_node <- "LUNG_CANCER"
bn_cv_acc <- numeric(10)

# 3. 10-Fold Cross-Validation Loop
for (i in 1:10) {
  val_idx    <- cv_folds[[i]]
  fold_train <- train_bn[val_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  fold_val   <- train_bn[-val_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Remove single-level columns if any exist in the fold
  single_level <- sapply(fold_train, function(x) length(unique(x)) < 2)
  if (any(single_level)) {
    fold_train <- fold_train[, !single_level, drop = FALSE]
    fold_val   <- fold_val[, intersect(names(fold_train), names(fold_val)), drop = FALSE]
  }
  
  # Harmonize factor levels between fold train and val
  for (col in names(fold_train)) {
    if (is.factor(fold_train[[col]])) {
      fold_val[[col]] <- factor(fold_val[[col]], levels = levels(fold_train[[col]]))
    }
  }
  
  # Learn structure and fit parameters
  fit_res <- tryCatch({
    dag <- hc(fold_train)
    bn.fit(dag, data = fold_train, method = "bayes", iss = 1)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (is.null(fit_res)) {
    bn_cv_acc[i] <- NA
    next
  }
  
  # Predict via likelihood weighting
  preds <- tryCatch({
    predict(fit_res, node = target_node, data = fold_val, method = "bayes-lw")
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (!is.null(preds)) {
    bn_cv_acc[i] <- mean(preds == fold_val[[target_node]], na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    bn_cv_acc[i] <- NA
  }
}

cat("BayesNet 10-Fold CV Mean Accuracy:", mean(bn_cv_acc, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# 4. Final Model Training and Test Evaluation
dag_final <- hc(train_bn)
bn_final  <- bn.fit(dag_final, data = train_bn, method = "bayes", iss = 1)

bn_preds <- predict(bn_final, node = target_node, data = test_bn, method = "bayes-lw")

confusionMatrix(bn_preds, test_bn[[target_node]], positive = "Yes")
```

## Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)

```{r}
library(LiblineaR)
library(caret)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Recode 0/1 to Valid R Variable Names ("No" / "Yes")
# ---------------------------------------------------------
train_sgd <- train_set
test_sgd <- test_set

if (!all(levels(train_sgd$LUNG_CANCER) %in% c("No", "Yes"))) {
  train_sgd$LUNG_CANCER <- factor(train_sgd$LUNG_CANCER, 
                                  levels = c("0", "1"), 
                                  labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  
  test_sgd$LUNG_CANCER  <- factor(test_sgd$LUNG_CANCER, 
                                  levels = c("0", "1"), 
                                  labels = c("No", "Yes"))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Configure trainControl
# ---------------------------------------------------------
train_ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  verboseIter = FALSE
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Train Regularized Logistic Regression (SGD Equivalent)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
sgd_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = train_sgd,
  method = "regLogistic",
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(
    cost = 1 / (1e-4 * nrow(train_sgd)),
    loss = "L2_dual",
    epsilon = 0.01
  ),
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  metric = "ROC"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Predict & Evaluate
# ---------------------------------------------------------
sgd_preds <- predict(sgd_model, newdata = test_sgd)

# positive = "Yes" matches the second factor level
conf_matrix_sgd <- confusionMatrix(sgd_preds, test_sgd$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
print(conf_matrix_sgd)
```

## Logistic Model Tree (LMT)
A Model-Based Recursive Partitioning Tree with Linear Regression is the alternative to Weka's LMT.

```{r warning=FALSE}
library(partykit)
library(pROC)

lmt_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha   = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10),
  minsize = c(15, 30, 50)
)

best_lmt_auc <- -1
best_lmt_params <- list(alpha = 0.05, minsize = 30)
formula_str <- as.formula(paste("LUNG_CANCER ~", paste(setdiff(names(train_set), "LUNG_CANCER"), collapse = " + ")))

set.seed(123)
for (g in seq_len(nrow(lmt_grid))) {
  curr_alpha   <- lmt_grid$alpha[g]
  curr_minsize <- lmt_grid$minsize[g]
  
  cv_auc <- numeric(10)
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tr_idx <- cv_folds[[i]]
    fold_train <- train_sgd[tr_idx, ]
    fold_val   <- train_sgd[-tr_idx, ]
    
    tree_fit <- tryCatch({
      glmtree(formula_str, data = fold_train, family = binomial, alpha = curr_alpha, minsize = curr_minsize)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    if (is.null(tree_fit)) {
      cv_auc[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    val_probs <- predict(tree_fit, newdata = fold_val, type = "response")
    cv_auc[i] <- as.numeric(roc(response = fold_val$LUNG_CANCER, predictor = val_probs, quiet = TRUE)$auc)
  }
  
  mean_auc <- mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.nan(mean_auc) && mean_auc > best_lmt_auc) {
    best_lmt_auc <- mean_auc
    best_lmt_params$alpha   <- curr_alpha
    best_lmt_params$minsize <- curr_minsize
  }
}

cat("Best LMT Params -> Alpha:", best_lmt_params$alpha, "| Minsize:", best_lmt_params$minsize, "with CV AUC:", best_lmt_auc, "\n")

# --- Final Model with Best Parameters ---
final_lmt <- glmtree(formula_str, data = train_sgd, family = binomial, alpha = best_lmt_params$alpha, minsize = best_lmt_params$minsize)
test_probs_lmt <- predict(final_lmt, newdata = test_sgd, type = "response")
test_preds_lmt <- factor(ifelse(test_probs_lmt >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
confusionMatrix(test_preds_lmt, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
```

## Random Forest

```{r}
# Calculate mtry (numFeatures = 0 defaults to sqrt(number of predictors))
num_predictors <- ncol(train_set) - 1
default_mtry <- floor(sqrt(num_predictors))

rf_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = train_sgd,
  method = "rf",
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  ntree = 100, # numIterations = 100
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(mtry = default_mtry), # numFeatures = 0 (default sqrt(p))
  nodesize = 1 # maxDepth = 0 (unconstrained depth, minimal node size)
)

# 1. Evaluate on holdout test set
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_sgd)
conf_matrix_rf <- confusionMatrix(rf_preds, test_sgd$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix_rf)
```


## Reduced Error Pruning Tree (REPTree)

```{r}
reptree_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = train_set,
  method = "rpart",
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(cp = 0.001), # minVarianceProp = 0.001
  control = rpart.control(
    minsplit = 2,  # minNum = 2.0
    minbucket = 2,
    maxdepth = 30  # maxDepth = -1 (unconstrained)
  )
)

# 1. Evaluate on holdout test set
reptree_preds <- predict(reptree_model, newdata = test_set)
conf_matrix_reptree <- confusionMatrix(reptree_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix_reptree)

# 2. Extract probabilities for downstream ROC curve step
prob_reptree <- predict(reptree_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
```

## Rotation Forest (RotF)

```{r}
library(rotationForest)
library(caret)
library(pROC)

# 1. Align factor levels and create dummy variables
for (col in names(train_set)) {
  if (is.factor(train_set[[col]])) {
    test_set[[col]] <- factor(test_set[[col]], levels = levels(train_set[[col]]))
  }
}

dummies <- dummyVars(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = train_set, fullRank = TRUE)
x_train_df <- as.data.frame(predict(dummies, newdata = train_set))
x_test_df  <- as.data.frame(predict(dummies, newdata = test_set))

colnames(x_train_df) <- make.names(colnames(x_train_df))
colnames(x_test_df)  <- make.names(colnames(x_test_df))

nzv <- nearZeroVar(x_train_df)
if (length(nzv) > 0) {
  x_train_df <- x_train_df[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
  x_test_df  <- x_test_df[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
}

x_test_df <- x_test_df[, colnames(x_train_df), drop = FALSE]

y_train_num <- ifelse(train_set$LUNG_CANCER == "Yes", 1L, 0L)
y_test_num  <- ifelse(test_set$LUNG_CANCER == "Yes", 1L, 0L)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Hyperparameter Grid Search via 10-Fold CV
# ---------------------------------------------------------
num_features <- ncol(x_train_df)

# Define a grid of hyperparameters to test
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  K = c(2, min(3, floor(num_features / 3)), 5),
  L = c(15, 25, 50)
)

best_auc <- -1
best_params <- list(K = 2, L = 25)

set.seed(123)
for (g in seq_len(nrow(param_grid))) {
  current_K <- param_grid$K[g]
  current_L <- param_grid$L[g]
  
  # Skip invalid configurations if K is too large for feature count
  if (current_K >= num_features) next 
  
  cv_auc <- numeric(10)
  
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tr_idx  <- cv_folds[[i]]
    
    fold_x_tr  <- x_train_df[tr_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    fold_y_tr  <- factor(y_train_num[tr_idx], levels = c(0, 1))
    fold_x_val <- x_train_df[-tr_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    fold_y_val <- y_train_num[-tr_idx]
    
    # Fit with current grid parameters
    rf_fit <- tryCatch({
      rotationForest(x = fold_x_tr, y = fold_y_tr, K = current_K, L = current_L)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    if (is.null(rf_fit)) {
      cv_auc[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    val_probs <- predict(rf_fit, newdata = fold_x_val)
    if (is.matrix(val_probs)) val_probs <- val_probs[, 2]
    
    actual_val <- factor(ifelse(fold_y_val == 1, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
    cv_auc[i] <- as.numeric(roc(response = actual_val, predictor = val_probs, quiet = TRUE)$auc)
  }
  
  mean_cv_auc <- mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Track the best performing hyperparameter combination
  if (!is.nan(mean_cv_auc) && mean_cv_auc > best_auc) {
    best_auc <- mean_cv_auc
    best_params$K <- current_K
    best_params$L <- current_L
  }
}

cat("Best Tuned Hyperparameters -> K:", best_params$K, "| L:", best_params$L, "with CV AUC:", best_auc, "\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Final Model Evaluation using TUNED Parameters
# ---------------------------------------------------------
final_rf <- rotationForest(
  x = x_train_df,
  y = factor(y_train_num, levels = c(0, 1)),
  K = best_params$K,
  L = best_params$L
)

test_probs <- predict(final_rf, newdata = x_test_df)
if (is.matrix(test_probs)) {
  test_probs <- test_probs[, 2]
}

test_preds_rotf <- factor(ifelse(test_probs >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
conf_matrix_rot <- confusionMatrix(test_preds_rotf, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
print(conf_matrix_rot)
```

## AdaBoostM1

```{r}
library(adabag)
library(pROC)

adaboost_grid <- expand.grid(
  mfinal = c(25, 50, 100)
)

best_ada_auc <- -1
best_ada_mfinal <- 50

set.seed(123)
for (g in seq_len(nrow(adaboost_grid))) {
  curr_mfinal <- adaboost_grid$mfinal[g]
  
  cv_auc <- numeric(10)
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tr_idx <- cv_folds[[i]]
    fold_train <- train_set[tr_idx, ]
    fold_val   <- train_set[-tr_idx, ]
    
    ada_fit <- tryCatch({
      boosting(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = fold_train, boos = FALSE, mfinal = curr_mfinal)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    if (is.null(ada_fit)) {
      cv_auc[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    ada_pred_obj <- predict.boosting(ada_fit, newdata = fold_val)
    pos_idx <- which(colnames(ada_pred_obj$prob) == "Yes")
    if (length(pos_idx) == 0) pos_idx <- 2
    val_probs <- ada_pred_obj$prob[, pos_idx]
    
    cv_auc[i] <- as.numeric(roc(response = fold_val$LUNG_CANCER, predictor = val_probs, quiet = TRUE)$auc)
  }
  
  mean_auc <- mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.nan(mean_auc) && mean_auc > best_ada_auc) {
    best_ada_auc <- mean_auc
    best_ada_mfinal <- curr_mfinal
  }
}

cat("Best AdaBoost Mfinal:", best_ada_mfinal, "with CV AUC:", best_ada_auc, "\n")

# --- Final Model with Best Parameters ---
adaboost_model <- boosting(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = train_set, boos = FALSE, mfinal = best_ada_mfinal)
adaboost_pred_obj <- predict.boosting(adaboost_model, newdata = test_set)

# 3. Extract positive class probabilities safely by column index
pos_class_index <- which(levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER) == "Yes")
prob_adaboost   <- adaboost_pred_obj$prob[, pos_class_index]

# 4. Generate hard class predictions & confusion matrix
adaboost_preds <- factor(adaboost_pred_obj$class, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
conf_matrix_adaboost <- confusionMatrix(adaboost_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix_adaboost)
```

## Majority Voting

```{r}
# --- MAJORITY VOTING ENSEMBLE ---

# 1. Collect all individual model predictions into a single data frame
# (Ensure they are all character or factor vectors of the same length)
voting_df <- data.frame(
  NB      = as.character(nb_preds),
  BayesNet= as.character(bn_preds),
  SGD     = as.character(sgd_preds),
  SVM     = as.character(svm_preds),
  LR      = as.character(glm_preds),
  ANN     = as.character(ann_preds),
  KNN     = as.character(knn_preds),
  C50     = as.character(c50_preds),
  RF      = as.character(rf_preds),
  RT      = as.character(rt_preds),
  REPTree = as.character(reptree_preds),
  LMT     = as.character(test_preds_lmt),
  RotF    = as.character(test_preds_rotf),
  Ada     = as.character(adaboost_preds),
  MLP     = as.character(mlp_preds),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 2. Tally votes for each row
target_levels <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER) # Use test_selected for Section 4
pos_class <- target_levels[2] # "Yes"
neg_class <- target_levels[1] # "No"

majority_preds_char <- apply(voting_df, 1, function(row) {
  # Count how many models predicted "Yes"
  yes_votes <- sum(row == pos_class, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Count how many models predicted "No"
  no_votes  <- sum(row == neg_class, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  if (yes_votes > no_votes) {
    return(pos_class)
  } else if (no_votes > yes_votes) {
    return(neg_class)
  } else {
    # Fallback for ties: default to negative class or a preferred model
    return(neg_class) 
  }
})

# 3. Convert back to a factor with the exact target levels
majority_preds <- factor(majority_preds_char, levels = target_levels)

# 4. Evaluate Performance via Confusion Matrix
conf_matrix_majority <- confusionMatrix(majority_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, positive = pos_class) # Use test_selected for Section 4
print(conf_matrix_majority)
```

## Stacking

```{r}
library(caretEnsemble)
# --- STACKING ENSEMBLE ---

# 1. Define specific train control for the ensemble base models
# (Ensures out-of-fold predictions are saved for the meta-learner)
stack_ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  verboseIter = FALSE
)

# 2. Train a diverse list of base models using caretList
set.seed(123)
model_list <- caretList(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ ., 
  data = train_set, # Use train_selected for Section 4
  trControl = stack_ctrl,
  methodList = c("glm", "knn"),
  metric = "ROC"
)

# Optional: Add tuned models to the list if desired (e.g., random forest)
# model_list$rf <- caret::train(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = train_set, method = "rf", trControl = stack_ctrl, metric = "ROC")

# 3. Create the Stacked Model (Meta-learner: Logistic Regression)
set.seed(123)
stack_model <- caretStack(
  model_list,
  method = "glm",
  metric = "ROC",
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = "cv",
    number = 5,
    classProbs = TRUE,
    summaryFunction = twoClassSummary
  )
)

# Print summary of the stacked model weights
print(stack_model)

# 4. Predict on Test Set & Evaluate
# Get probability of the positive class ("Yes")
stack_probs <- predict(stack_model, newdata = test_set) # Use test_selected for Section 4

yes <- stack_probs$Yes
stack_preds <- c()
for (i in seq(1:length(yes))) {
  if (yes[[i]] > 0.5) {
    stack_preds <- c(stack_preds, "Yes")
  } else {
    stack_preds <- c(stack_preds, "No")
  }
}

stack_preds <- factor(stack_preds, levels=levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))

# Confusion Matrix Evaluation
conf_matrix_stack <- confusionMatrix(stack_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
print(conf_matrix_stack)

# 5. Save objects for your final ROC curve and Metrics Table loops
prob_stack <- stack_probs
```

## Evaluation Metrics Table

```{r}
library(knitr)

# Define positive class label (e.g., "YES" or "1")
positive_class <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)[2]

neg_class <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)[1]

rotf_preds <- factor(
  ifelse(prob_rotf > 0.5, positive_class, neg_class),
  levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)
)

# --- Helper Function to Extract Metrics safely from Confusion Matrix ---
get_metrics <- function(predictions, actual, pos_class) {
  cm <- confusionMatrix(predictions, actual, positive = pos_class)
  
  acc <- cm$overall["Accuracy"]
  prec <- cm$byClass["Precision"]
  rec  <- cm$byClass["Sensitivity"] # Sensitivity = Recall
  
  return(c(Accuracy = unname(acc), Precision = unname(prec), Recall = unname(rec)))
}

# --- Compile Predictions from All Models ---
# Assumes each model's predicted class factor vector is stored from earlier steps:
# Correct "Naive Bayes" test prediction
nb_preds <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_set)

# Set predictions to the proper format
target_levels <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER) # e.g., c("No", "Yes")

# Robust mapper to align all predictions to the exact reference levels
align_to_reference <- function(preds, ref_levels) {
  # Convert to character first to safely examine values
  preds_char <- as.character(preds)
  
  # Check if predictions are 0/1 while reference is No/Yes
  if (all(preds_char %in% c("0", "1", NA)) && all(ref_levels %in% c("No", "Yes"))) {
    preds_char <- ifelse(preds_char == "1", "Yes", "No")
  }
  # Check if predictions are No/Yes while reference is 0/1
  else if (all(preds_char %in% c("No", "Yes", NA)) && all(ref_levels %in% c("0", "1"))) {
    preds_char <- ifelse(preds_char == "Yes", "1", "0")
  }
  
  # Return factor with identical level structure
  factor(preds_char, levels = ref_levels)
}

models_preds <- list(
  "Naive Bayes"         = nb_preds,
  "BayesNet"            = bn_preds,
  "SGD"                 = sgd_preds,
  "Linear SVM"          = svm_preds,
  "Logistic Regression" = glm_preds,
  "ANN"                 = ann_preds,
  "KNN (K=3)"           = knn_preds,
  "C5.0 Tree"           = c50_preds,
  "Random Forest"       = rf_preds,
  "Random Tree"         = rt_preds,
  "REPTree"             = reptree_preds,
  "LMT (glmtree)"       = test_preds_lmt,
  "Rotation Forest"     = test_preds_rotf,
  "AdaBoost.M1"         = adaboost_preds,
  "ML Perceptron"       = mlp_preds,
  "Majority Voting"     = majority_preds,
  "Stacking"            = stack_preds
)

# Standardize all model prediction vectors to the reference levels
models_preds_clean <- lapply(models_preds, function(p) {
  align_to_reference(p, ref_levels = target_levels)
})

# Make sure pos_class matches an existing level in test_set
pos_class <- if ("Yes" %in% target_levels) "Yes" else target_levels[2]

# Compute metrics safely
results_list <- lapply(models_preds_clean, function(preds) {
  get_metrics(preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, pos_class = pos_class)
})

results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
print(results_df)
```

```{r}
  ) %>%
```

All models performed similarly. We will choose the best ones to test against feature selection: BayesNet (top accuracy and precision), LMT (2nd in accuracy and 1st in recall, SVM is removed because these models are functionally the same and SVM performed much worse in AUC), logistic regression, rotation forest, ML perceptron, and ANN (very high recall).

## Bayesian Network (BayesNet)

```{r}
library(bnlearn)
library(pROC)
library(caret)

# 1. Prepare data frames
train_bn <- train_selected
test_bn  <- test_selected

# Ensure BMI is numeric before discretizing
train_bn$BMI <- as.numeric(train_bn$BMI)
test_bn$BMI  <- as.numeric(test_bn$BMI)

# Factorize all other categorical/symptom columns
factor_cols <- setdiff(names(train_bn), c("BMI", "LUNG_CANCER"))
train_bn[factor_cols] <- lapply(train_bn[factor_cols], factor)
test_bn[factor_cols]  <- lapply(test_bn[factor_cols], factor)

# 2. Discretize BMI into 3 quantile bins using bnlearn
train_bn["BMI"] <- bnlearn::discretize(
  data = train_bn["BMI"],
  method = "quantile",
  breaks = 3,
  ordered = FALSE
)

# Project training quantile boundaries onto test_selected$BMI
raw_train_vals <- as.numeric(train_selected$BMI)
brks <- quantile(raw_train_vals, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 4), na.rm = TRUE)
brks[1] <- -Inf
brks[length(brks)] <- Inf

test_bn$BMI <- cut(
  as.numeric(test_selected$BMI),
  breaks = brks,
  labels = levels(train_bn$BMI),
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

# Ensure test_bn factor levels match train_bn perfectly
for (col in names(train_bn)) {
  if (is.factor(train_bn[[col]])) {
    test_bn[[col]] <- factor(test_bn[[col]], levels = levels(train_bn[[col]]))
  }
}

target_node <- "LUNG_CANCER"
bn_cv_acc <- numeric(10)

# 3. 10-Fold Cross-Validation Loop
for (i in 1:10) {
  val_idx    <- cv_folds[[i]]
  fold_train <- train_bn[val_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  fold_val   <- train_bn[-val_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Remove single-level columns if any exist in the fold
  single_level <- sapply(fold_train, function(x) length(unique(x)) < 2)
  if (any(single_level)) {
    fold_train <- fold_train[, !single_level, drop = FALSE]
    fold_val   <- fold_val[, intersect(names(fold_train), names(fold_val)), drop = FALSE]
  }
  
  # Harmonize factor levels between fold train and val
  for (col in names(fold_train)) {
    if (is.factor(fold_train[[col]])) {
      fold_val[[col]] <- factor(fold_val[[col]], levels = levels(fold_train[[col]]))
    }
  }
  
  # Learn structure and fit parameters
  fit_res <- tryCatch({
    dag <- hc(fold_train)
    bn.fit(dag, data = fold_train, method = "bayes", iss = 1)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (is.null(fit_res)) {
    bn_cv_acc[i] <- NA
    next
  }
  
  # Predict via likelihood weighting
  preds <- tryCatch({
    predict(fit_res, node = target_node, data = fold_val, method = "bayes-lw")
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (!is.null(preds)) {
    bn_cv_acc[i] <- mean(preds == fold_val[[target_node]], na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    bn_cv_acc[i] <- NA
  }
}

cat("BayesNet 10-Fold CV Mean Accuracy:", mean(bn_cv_acc, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# 4. Final Model Training and Test Evaluation
dag_final <- hc(train_bn)
bn_final  <- bn.fit(dag_final, data = train_bn, method = "bayes", iss = 1)

bn_preds <- predict(bn_final, node = target_node, data = test_bn, method = "bayes-lw")

confusionMatrix(bn_preds, test_bn[[target_node]], positive = "Yes")
```

## Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)

```{r}
library(LiblineaR)
library(caret)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Recode 0/1 to Valid R Variable Names ("No" / "Yes")
# ---------------------------------------------------------
train_sgd_selected <- train_selected
test_sgd_selected <- test_selected

if (!all(levels(train_sgd_selected$LUNG_CANCER) %in% c("No", "Yes"))) {
  train_sgd_selected$LUNG_CANCER <- factor(train_sgd_selected$LUNG_CANCER, 
                                  levels = c("0", "1"), 
                                  labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  
  test_sgd_selected$LUNG_CANCER  <- factor(test_sgd_selected$LUNG_CANCER, 
                                  levels = c("0", "1"), 
                                  labels = c("No", "Yes"))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Configure trainControl
# ---------------------------------------------------------
train_ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  verboseIter = FALSE
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Train Regularized Logistic Regression (SGD Equivalent)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
sgd_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = train_sgd_selected,
  method = "regLogistic",
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(
    cost = 1 / (1e-4 * nrow(train_sgd_selected)),
    loss = "L2_dual",
    epsilon = 0.01
  ),
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  metric = "ROC"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Predict & Evaluate
# ---------------------------------------------------------
sgd_preds <- predict(sgd_model, newdata = test_sgd_selected)

# positive = "Yes" matches the second factor level
conf_matrix_sgd <- confusionMatrix(sgd_preds, test_sgd_selected$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
print(conf_matrix_sgd)
```

## Logistic Model Tree (LMT)
A Model-Based Recursive Partitioning Tree with Linear Regression is the alternative to Weka's LMT.

```{r warning=FALSE}
library(partykit)
library(pROC)

lmt_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha   = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10),
  minsize = c(15, 30, 50)
)

best_lmt_auc <- -1
best_lmt_params <- list(alpha = 0.05, minsize = 30)
formula_str <- as.formula(paste("LUNG_CANCER ~", paste(setdiff(names(train_selected), "LUNG_CANCER"), collapse = " + ")))

set.seed(123)
for (g in seq_len(nrow(lmt_grid))) {
  curr_alpha   <- lmt_grid$alpha[g]
  curr_minsize <- lmt_grid$minsize[g]
  
  cv_auc <- numeric(10)
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tr_idx <- cv_folds[[i]]
    fold_train <- train_sgd_selected[tr_idx, ]
    fold_val   <- train_sgd_selected[-tr_idx, ]
    
    tree_fit <- tryCatch({
      glmtree(formula_str, data = fold_train, family = binomial, alpha = curr_alpha, minsize = curr_minsize)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    if (is.null(tree_fit)) {
      cv_auc[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    val_probs <- predict(tree_fit, newdata = fold_val, type = "response")
    cv_auc[i] <- as.numeric(roc(response = fold_val$LUNG_CANCER, predictor = val_probs, quiet = TRUE)$auc)
  }
  
  mean_auc <- mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.nan(mean_auc) && mean_auc > best_lmt_auc) {
    best_lmt_auc <- mean_auc
    best_lmt_params$alpha   <- curr_alpha
    best_lmt_params$minsize <- curr_minsize
  }
}

cat("Best LMT Params -> Alpha:", best_lmt_params$alpha, "| Minsize:", best_lmt_params$minsize, "with CV AUC:", best_lmt_auc, "\n")

# --- Final Model with Best Parameters ---
final_lmt <- glmtree(formula_str, data = train_sgd_selected, family = binomial, alpha = best_lmt_params$alpha, minsize = best_lmt_params$minsize)
test_probs_lmt <- predict(final_lmt, newdata = test_sgd_selected, type = "response")
test_preds_lmt <- factor(ifelse(test_probs_lmt >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
confusionMatrix(test_preds_lmt, test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
```

## Rotation Forest (RotF)

```{r}
library(rotationForest)
library(caret)
library(pROC)

# 1. Align factor levels and create dummy variables
for (col in names(train_selected)) {
  if (is.factor(train_selected[[col]])) {
    test_selected[[col]] <- factor(test_selected[[col]], levels = levels(train_selected[[col]]))
  }
}

dummies <- dummyVars(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = train_selected, fullRank = TRUE)
x_train_df <- as.data.frame(predict(dummies, newdata = train_selected))
x_test_df  <- as.data.frame(predict(dummies, newdata = test_selected))

colnames(x_train_df) <- make.names(colnames(x_train_df))
colnames(x_test_df)  <- make.names(colnames(x_test_df))

nzv <- nearZeroVar(x_train_df)
if (length(nzv) > 0) {
  x_train_df <- x_train_df[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
  x_test_df  <- x_test_df[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
}

x_test_df <- x_test_df[, colnames(x_train_df), drop = FALSE]

y_train_num <- ifelse(train_selected$LUNG_CANCER == "Yes", 1L, 0L)
y_test_num  <- ifelse(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER == "Yes", 1L, 0L)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Hyperparameter Grid Search via 10-Fold CV
# ---------------------------------------------------------
num_features <- ncol(x_train_df)

# Define a grid of hyperparameters to test
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  K = c(2, min(3, floor(num_features / 3)), 5),
  L = c(15, 25, 50)
)

best_auc <- -1
best_params <- list(K = 2, L = 25)

set.seed(123)
for (g in seq_len(nrow(param_grid))) {
  current_K <- param_grid$K[g]
  current_L <- param_grid$L[g]
  
  # Skip invalid configurations if K is too large for feature count
  if (current_K >= num_features) next 
  
  cv_auc <- numeric(10)
  
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tr_idx  <- cv_folds[[i]]
    
    fold_x_tr  <- x_train_df[tr_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    fold_y_tr  <- factor(y_train_num[tr_idx], levels = c(0, 1))
    fold_x_val <- x_train_df[-tr_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    fold_y_val <- y_train_num[-tr_idx]
    
    # Fit with current grid parameters
    rf_fit <- tryCatch({
      rotationForest(x = fold_x_tr, y = fold_y_tr, K = current_K, L = current_L)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    if (is.null(rf_fit)) {
      cv_auc[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    val_probs <- predict(rf_fit, newdata = fold_x_val)
    if (is.matrix(val_probs)) val_probs <- val_probs[, 2]
    
    actual_val <- factor(ifelse(fold_y_val == 1, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
    cv_auc[i] <- as.numeric(roc(response = actual_val, predictor = val_probs, quiet = TRUE)$auc)
  }
  
  mean_cv_auc <- mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Track the best performing hyperparameter combination
  if (!is.nan(mean_cv_auc) && mean_cv_auc > best_auc) {
    best_auc <- mean_cv_auc
    best_params$K <- current_K
    best_params$L <- current_L
  }
}

cat("Best Tuned Hyperparameters -> K:", best_params$K, "| L:", best_params$L, "with CV AUC:", best_auc, "\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Final Model Evaluation using TUNED Parameters
# ---------------------------------------------------------
final_rf <- rotationForest(
  x = x_train_df,
  y = factor(y_train_num, levels = c(0, 1)),
  K = best_params$K,
  L = best_params$L
)

test_probs <- predict(final_rf, newdata = x_test_df)
if (is.matrix(test_probs)) {
  test_probs <- test_probs[, 2]
}

test_preds_rotf <- factor(ifelse(test_probs >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
conf_matrix_rot <- confusionMatrix(test_preds_rotf, test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
print(conf_matrix_rot)
```

## AdaBoostM1

```{r}
library(adabag)
library(pROC)

adaboost_grid <- expand.grid(
  mfinal = c(25, 50, 100)
)

best_ada_auc <- -1
best_ada_mfinal <- 50

set.seed(123)
for (g in seq_len(nrow(adaboost_grid))) {
  curr_mfinal <- adaboost_grid$mfinal[g]
  
  cv_auc <- numeric(10)
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tr_idx <- cv_folds[[i]]
    fold_train <- train_selected[tr_idx, ]
    fold_val   <- train_selected[-tr_idx, ]
    
    ada_fit <- tryCatch({
      boosting(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = fold_train, boos = FALSE, mfinal = curr_mfinal)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    if (is.null(ada_fit)) {
      cv_auc[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    ada_pred_obj <- predict.boosting(ada_fit, newdata = fold_val)
    pos_idx <- which(colnames(ada_pred_obj$prob) == "Yes")
    if (length(pos_idx) == 0) pos_idx <- 2
    val_probs <- ada_pred_obj$prob[, pos_idx]
    
    cv_auc[i] <- as.numeric(roc(response = fold_val$LUNG_CANCER, predictor = val_probs, quiet = TRUE)$auc)
  }
  
  mean_auc <- mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.nan(mean_auc) && mean_auc > best_ada_auc) {
    best_ada_auc <- mean_auc
    best_ada_mfinal <- curr_mfinal
  }
}

cat("Best AdaBoost Mfinal:", best_ada_mfinal, "with CV AUC:", best_ada_auc, "\n")

# --- Final Model with Best Parameters ---
adaboost_model <- boosting(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = train_selected, boos = FALSE, mfinal = best_ada_mfinal)
adaboost_pred_obj <- predict.boosting(adaboost_model, newdata = test_selected)

# 3. Extract positive class probabilities safely by column index
pos_class_index <- which(levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER) == "Yes")
prob_adaboost   <- adaboost_pred_obj$prob[, pos_class_index]

# 4. Generate hard class predictions & confusion matrix
adaboost_preds <- factor(adaboost_pred_obj$class, levels = levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER))
conf_matrix_adaboost <- confusionMatrix(adaboost_preds, test_selected$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix_adaboost)
```

## Majority Voting

```{r}
# --- MAJORITY VOTING ENSEMBLE ---

# 1. Collect all individual model predictions into a single data frame
# (Ensure they are all character or factor vectors of the same length)
voting_df <- data.frame(
  NB      = as.character(nb_preds),
  BayesNet= as.character(bn_preds),
  SGD     = as.character(sgd_preds),
  SVM     = as.character(svm_preds),
  LR      = as.character(glm_preds),
  ANN     = as.character(ann_preds),
  KNN     = as.character(knn_preds),
  C50     = as.character(c50_preds),
  RF      = as.character(rf_preds),
  RT      = as.character(rt_preds),
  REPTree = as.character(reptree_preds),
  LMT     = as.character(test_preds_lmt),
  RotF    = as.character(test_preds_rotf),
  Ada     = as.character(adaboost_preds),
  MLP     = as.character(mlp_preds),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 2. Tally votes for each row
target_levels <- levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER) # Use test_selected for Section 4
pos_class <- target_levels[2] # "Yes"
neg_class <- target_levels[1] # "No"

majority_preds_char <- apply(voting_df, 1, function(row) {
  # Count how many models predicted "Yes"
  yes_votes <- sum(row == pos_class, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Count how many models predicted "No"
  no_votes  <- sum(row == neg_class, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  if (yes_votes > no_votes) {
    return(pos_class)
  } else if (no_votes > yes_votes) {
    return(neg_class)
  } else {
    # Fallback for ties: default to negative class or a preferred model
    return(neg_class) 
  }
})

# 3. Convert back to a factor with the exact target levels
majority_preds <- factor(majority_preds_char, levels = target_levels)

# 4. Evaluate Performance via Confusion Matrix
conf_matrix_majority <- confusionMatrix(majority_preds, test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, positive = pos_class) # Use test_selected for Section 4
print(conf_matrix_majority)
```

## Stacking

```{r}
library(caretEnsemble)
# --- STACKING ENSEMBLE ---

# 1. Define specific train control for the ensemble base models
# (Ensures out-of-fold predictions are saved for the meta-learner)
stack_ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  verboseIter = FALSE
)

# 2. Train a diverse list of base models using caretList
set.seed(123)
model_list <- caretList(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ ., 
  data = train_set, # Use train_selected for Section 4
  trControl = stack_ctrl,
  methodList = c("glm", "knn"),
  metric = "ROC"
)

# Optional: Add tuned models to the list if desired (e.g., random forest)
# model_list$rf <- caret::train(LUNG_CANCER ~ ., data = train_set, method = "rf", trControl = stack_ctrl, metric = "ROC")

# 3. Create the Stacked Model (Meta-learner: Logistic Regression)
set.seed(123)
stack_model <- caretStack(
  model_list,
  method = "glm",
  metric = "ROC",
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = "cv",
    number = 5,
    classProbs = TRUE,
    summaryFunction = twoClassSummary
  )
)

# Print summary of the stacked model weights
print(stack_model)

# 4. Predict on Test Set & Evaluate
# Get probability of the positive class ("Yes")
stack_probs <- predict(stack_model, newdata = test_set) # Use test_selected for Section 4

yes <- stack_probs$Yes
stack_preds <- c()
for (i in seq(1:length(yes))) {
  if (yes[[i]] > 0.5) {
    stack_preds <- c(stack_preds, "Yes")
  } else {
    stack_preds <- c(stack_preds, "No")
  }
}

stack_preds <- factor(stack_preds, levels=levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))

# Confusion Matrix Evaluation
conf_matrix_stack <- confusionMatrix(stack_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, positive = "Yes")
print(conf_matrix_stack)
```

```{r}
# --- Model 1: AdaBoost ---

# Dynamically map the positive_class to the correct column in the prob matrix
# (Works whether the column name is "Yes", "1", or another value)
pos_class_index <- which(colnames(adaboost_pred_obj$prob) == positive_class)
# Fallback in case levels mismatch (e.g. searching for 'Yes' but matrix labeled '1')

    # Assume 2nd column as standard binary target if label isn't found
    pos_class_index <- 2 
}
prob_adaboost <- adaboost_pred_obj$prob[, pos_class_index]

# --- Model 2: BayesNet (bnlearn) ---
prob_bn_raw <- predict(bn_final, node = "LUNG_CANCER", data = test_bn, prob = TRUE)
if (!is.null(attr(prob_bn_raw, "prob"))) {
  prob_bn <- attr(prob_bn_raw, "prob")[positive_class, ]
} else {
  # Fallback if attribute wasn't populated or predictions were discrete classes
  prob_bn <- as.numeric(prob_bn_raw == positive_class)
}

# --- Model 3: Logistic Model Tree (glmtree / LMT) ---
if (inherits(final_lmt, "train")) {
  # If trained via caret custom method
  prob_lmt <- predict(final_lmt, newdata = test_selected, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
} else {
  # If trained directly via partykit::glmtree
  prob_lmt <- as.numeric(predict(final_lmt, newdata = test_selected, type = "response"))
}

# For majority voting
prob_majority <- c()
for (i in seq(1:324)) {
  value <- sum(prob_nb[[i]], prob_bn[[i]], prob_sgd[[i]], prob_svm[[i]], prob_lr[[i]], prob_ann[[i]], prob_knn[[i]], prob_dt[[i]], prob_rf[[i]], prob_rt[[i]], prob_reptree[[i]], prob_lmt[[i]], prob_rotf[[i]], prob_adaboost[[i]], prob_mlp[[i]]) / 15
  prob_majority <- c(prob_majority, value)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate pROC Objects
# ---------------------------------------------------------
target_levels <- levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER)

roc_nb       <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_nb,       levels = target_levels)
roc_bn       <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_bn,       levels = target_levels)
roc_sgd      <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_sgd,      levels = target_levels)
roc_svm      <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_svm,      levels = target_levels)
roc_lr       <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_lr,       levels = target_levels)
roc_ann      <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_ann,      levels = target_levels)
roc_knn      <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_knn,      levels = target_levels)
roc_dt       <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_dt,       levels = target_levels)
roc_lmt      <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_lmt,      levels = target_levels)
roc_rf       <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_rf,       levels = target_levels)
roc_rt       <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_rt,       levels = target_levels)
roc_rotf     <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_rotf,     levels = target_levels)
roc_adaboost <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_adaboost, levels = target_levels)
roc_mlp      <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_mlp,      levels = target_levels)
roc_stack    <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_majority, levels = target_levels)
roc_stack    <- roc(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, prob_stack,    levels = target_levels)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Plot Overlaying ROC Curves with AUC in Legend
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare model list, colors, and line widths
models <- list(
  "BayesNet"           = roc_nb,
  "Naive Bayes"        = roc_bn,
  "SGD"                = roc_sgd,
  "Linear SVM"         = roc_svm,
  "Logistic Reg."      = roc_lr,
  "ANN"                = roc_ann,
  "KNN"                = roc_knn,
  "Decision Tree"      = roc_dt,
  "LMT"                = roc_lmt,
  "Random Forest"      = roc_rf,
  "Random Tree"        = roc_rt,
  "Rotation Forest"    = roc_rotf,
  "AdaBoost"           = roc_adaboost,
  "MLP"                = roc_mlp,
  "Majority Voting"    = roc_majority,
  "Stacking"           = roc_stack
)

colors <- c(
  "red", "blue", "green3", "purple", "orange", 
  "brown", "hotpink", "darkcyan", "darkgreen", 
  "chartreuse4", "maroon", "black", "navy", "cyan3", "lightblue", "grey"
)

# Base canvas with first model
plot(
  roc_nb, 
  col = colors[1], 
  lwd = 2, 
  legacy.axes = TRUE,
  main = "ROC Curves Comparison Across Models",
  xlab = "False Positive Rate (1 - Specificity)",
  ylab = "True Positive Rate (Sensitivity)"
)

# Add remaining models
for (i in 2:length(models)) {
  plot(models[[i]], col = colors[i], lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
}

# Construct legend with AUC scores
auc_labels <- sapply(names(models), function(m) {
  sprintf("%s (AUC = %.3f)", m, as.numeric(models[[m]]$auc))
})

legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = auc_labels,
  col = colors,
  lwd = 2,
  cex = 0.65,
  bty = "n"
)
```

## Evaluation Metrics Table

```{r}
library(knitr)

# Define positive class label (e.g., "YES" or "1")
positive_class <- levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER)[2]

neg_class <- levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER)[1]

rotf_preds <- factor(
  ifelse(prob_rotf > 0.5, positive_class, neg_class),
  levels = levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER)
)

# --- Helper Function to Extract Metrics safely from Confusion Matrix ---
get_metrics <- function(predictions, actual, pos_class) {
  cm <- confusionMatrix(predictions, actual, positive = pos_class)
  
  acc <- cm$overall["Accuracy"]
  prec <- cm$byClass["Precision"]
  rec  <- cm$byClass["Sensitivity"] # Sensitivity = Recall
  
  return(c(Accuracy = unname(acc), Precision = unname(prec), Recall = unname(rec)))
}

# --- Compile Predictions from All Models ---
# Assumes each model's predicted class factor vector is stored from earlier steps:
# Correct "Naive Bayes" test prediction
nb_preds <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_selected)

# Set predictions to the proper format
target_levels <- levels(test_selected$LUNG_CANCER) # e.g., c("No", "Yes")

# Robust mapper to align all predictions to the exact reference levels
align_to_reference <- function(preds, ref_levels) {
  # Convert to character first to safely examine values
  preds_char <- as.character(preds)
  
  # Check if predictions are 0/1 while reference is No/Yes
  if (all(preds_char %in% c("0", "1", NA)) && all(ref_levels %in% c("No", "Yes"))) {
    preds_char <- ifelse(preds_char == "1", "Yes", "No")
  }
  # Check if predictions are No/Yes while reference is 0/1
  else if (all(preds_char %in% c("No", "Yes", NA)) && all(ref_levels %in% c("0", "1"))) {
    preds_char <- ifelse(preds_char == "Yes", "1", "0")
  }
  
  # Return factor with identical level structure
  factor(preds_char, levels = ref_levels)
}

models_preds <- list(
  "Naive Bayes"         = nb_preds,
  "BayesNet"            = bn_preds,
  "SGD"                 = sgd_preds,
  "Linear SVM"          = svm_preds,
  "Logistic Regression" = glm_preds,
  "ANN"                 = ann_preds,
  "KNN (K=3)"           = knn_preds,
  "C5.0 Tree"           = c50_preds,
  "Random Forest"       = rf_preds,
  "Random Tree"         = rt_preds,
  "REPTree"             = reptree_preds,
  "LMT (glmtree)"       = test_preds_lmt,
  "Rotation Forest"     = test_preds_rotf,
  "AdaBoost.M1"         = adaboost_preds,
  "ML Perceptron"       = mlp_preds,
  "Majority Voting"     = majority_preds,
  "Stacking"            = stack_preds
)

# Standardize all model prediction vectors to the reference levels
models_preds_clean <- lapply(models_preds, function(p) {
  align_to_reference(p, ref_levels = target_levels)
})

# Make sure pos_class matches an existing level in test_selected
pos_class <- if ("Yes" %in% target_levels) "Yes" else target_levels[2]

# Compute metrics safely
results_list <- lapply(models_preds_clean, function(preds) {
  get_metrics(preds, test_selected$LUNG_CANCER, pos_class = pos_class)
})

results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
print(results_df)
```

## Selection vs. No Selection

```{r}
results_compare <- results_unselected %>%
  left_join(results_selected, by=join_by(Model==Model)) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  rename("AccuracyAll"=Accuracy.x,
         "AccuracySelect"=Accuracy.y,
         "PrecisionAll"=Precision.x,
         "PrecisionSelect"=Precision.y,
         "RecallAll"=Recall.x,
         "RecallSelect"=Recall.y,
         "F1All"=`F1 Score.x`,
         "F1Select"=`F1 Score.y`) %>%
  mutate(AccuracyDif = AccuracySelect - AccuracyAll,
         PrecisionDif = PrecisionSelect - PrecisionAll,
         RecallDif = RecallSelect - RecallAll,
         F1Dif = F1Select - F1All)
```

```{r}

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(scales)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Calculate a shared color scale across all metric columns
metric_cols <- c("AccuracyDif", "PrecisionDif", "RecallDif", "F1Dif")

all_values <- unlist(results_compare[metric_cols], use.names = FALSE)
all_values <- as.numeric(all_values)
all_values <- all_values[!is.na(all_values)]

# Define color boundaries
color_min <- -0.2
color_max <-  0.2

# Define the continuous gradient
color_fn <- col_numeric(
  palette = c("#d73027", "#f7f7f7", "#1a9850"),
  domain = c(color_min, color_max),
  na.color = "transparent"
)

# Apply gradient to individual values
true_gradient_scale <- function(x) {
  x_num <- as.numeric(x)

  sapply(x_num, function(val) {

    if (is.na(val)) {
      return("NA")
    }

    # Clamp values to the specified color boundaries
    clamped_val <- max(color_min, min(color_max, val))

    # Calculate color using the clamped value
    bg_color <- color_fn(clamped_val)

    # Display the ORIGINAL value, not the clamped value
    sprintf(
      '<span style="display:block; padding:4px;
       background-color:%s; border-radius:3px;">%.4f</span>',
      bg_color,
      val
    )
  })
}

# 4. Apply formatting to the comparison table
results_compare_colored <- results_compare %>%
  select(Model, all_of(metric_cols)) %>%
  arrange(Model) %>%
  mutate(
    across(all_of(metric_cols), true_gradient_scale)
  )

# 5. Render the HTML table
kable_table_compare <- kable(
  results_compare_colored,
  escape = FALSE,
  caption = "<b>Performance Comparison for All Models</b>",
  col.names = c("Model", "Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall", "F1 Score"),
  align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c")
)

print(kable_table_compare)
```
